cpuThrottle.scope: openProbe and after-open counters precede CPU throttling; subsequent netplay setup and first game callback use the configured per-side rates.

headedLaunch.scope: Window-mode environment control, not a production code change; proxy, input, audio/context, CPU setup, and native GPU arguments are unchanged.

scopes.body: Every original sample in [first frontier >= startFrame, first frontier >= endFrame); no phase or rewound-cursor filtering. Without a terminal crossing the observed body is right-censored.
scopes.progress: Closed Hz and cumulative counter deltas use endpoint minus start, including the endpoint counters. The endpoint callback cost belongs to tail; body cost includes start. Missing native frontier uses explicitly labelled observed next high-water, never captures, and complete stays false.
scopes.gaps: Top-level gap fields retain body-only submission/RAF timestamp semantics. formalWithEndBoundary also closes through the terminal marker. Cross-boundary intervals and all sampled startup/tail costs remain separate. No sample is removed from raw results.
scopes.timing: callbackCompletionGapMs is the post-native sampledAt gap between renderer submissions, not whole observer callback return; RAF timestamps and submissions are not physical scanout.
scopes.phase: scenes is a compatibility alias of sessionPhases (SessionPhase, not internal MatchScene); no phase is excluded.
scopes.capture: captures is a once-only input-capture counter and may be ahead of simulation completion; it never chooses boundaries.
scopes.nativeWork: callbackWorkMs is the existing native game callback measurement, not total JavaScript observer time or GPU completion.

plannedInjectionPartitions.rule: Half-open before/during/after by post-native endpoint converted to relay performance.now; every formal body callback belongs to one partition. After includes delayed packet delivery and braking decay.

Pre/post history is at most 32 actual polls each, not a guaranteed duration; omitted polls and final pending are retained explicitly.

metadata.scope: Owned loopback shared relay; JS receive/forward/send API boundaries, not OS or peer delivery.

injection.packetScope: E9NP version 4 kind 1; ACK-only and redundant input included; non-input control/hash/signaling untouched; relay has no separate RTC repair lane.
injection.jitterAlgorithm: Per-sender LCG 1664525*x+1013904223, seed 0x915ab+sender; same formula as legacy client impairment. Relay forwarding order can differ.
injection.burstClock: First non-empty E9NP input receive in this relay process; distinct from browser active time.

clockMapping.limitation: Numerical mapping only; no separately calibrated cross-process error. No peer receive/native acceptance/physical scanout timestamp is inferred.

plannedInjection.classification: Half-open configured relay interval; exact per-packet burst flags separately retained

relay.timingScope: Existing relay probe heartbeat/timer observations, not a peer network heartbeat or OS arrival.

metadata.scope: Read-only host CPU counters and candidate process CPU counters. No performance samples are excluded or reweighted.
limitations: Aggregate CPU occupancy does not establish single-core availability, CPU frequency, thermal state, GPU load, or a stable benchmark environment.
Process names are candidates for contention, not proof that a process is compiling. Known harness/relay/helper PIDs are labeled separately; other node processes remain unlabeled candidates.
Process CPU is cumulative lifetime CPU seconds. A first sighting is not CPU consumed during this run; PID reuse or counter reset can break a delta.
The 5 s process snapshots miss short tasks that start and exit between snapshots. Timer delays and source/receive times are retained.
This observer has overhead. Its own PowerShell helper is intentionally not a candidate process, but its work is included in aggregate CPU counters.
Overflow and sampling failures make this evidence incomplete; they are never a reason to silently remove a game result.

host.limitations: Persistent PowerShell Get-Process helper; no per-query process launch assumed. CPU points lack a before/after read bracket. 1s/5s sampling cannot assign short pauses to processes.

launches.method: CDP SystemInfo.getProcessInfo browser PID + single-PID Win32_Process CIM
launches.commandLineHashEncoding: UTF-8 of the exact Win32_Process.CommandLine string

launches.method: CDP SystemInfo.getProcessInfo browser PID + single-PID Win32_Process CIM
launches.commandLineHashEncoding: UTF-8 of the exact Win32_Process.CommandLine string

headedControl.scope: Only the two browsers created by this harness. CDP supplies the unique browser PID; CIM reads only that PID. Save only command-line SHA256 and allowlisted flags, never raw command lines, executable/profile paths, or process lists. Missing identity observation is explicit and cannot establish a matched environment control. Window bounds, visibility/focus and existing lifecycle events do not prove physical scanout, continuous foreground visibility, or non-overlap. No window is moved or brought to front.

definitions.scale: Recorded callback-end observation, not necessarily scale used on callback entry
definitions.timing: RAF timestamp, actual RAF entry/exit and post-native sample are separate clocks/boundaries; onGameFrame entry is an observer hook, not native entry. No subtraction from RAF gap to infer idle.

limitations: No performance acceptance or causal attribution follows from correctness/checks passing.
All unresolved response intents and all source checks remain intact; missing values are not zero latency.
A finite 250ms anomaly probe with no eligible episode does not establish smoothness and can miss 103ms issues by design.
This wall-clock burst workload is not an AB comparison with E1 tape or the old burst.
Before/during/after are planned injection phases; delayed input delivery and brake decay can continue after the configured period.
